purpose: Decoded semantic expectations authored from accepted design, exact upstream API references, and released public contracts without consulting target implementation output.

owners.accountability: Owns rationale, limitations, causal discrimination, and successor review; may not implement or derive expectations from production providers, compilers, query execution, or release output.

global_limitations: These decoded rows are a minimal discriminating corpus, not proof that unrepresented programs have identical semantics.
Provider expectations are bound to the exact referenced versions and must be superseded, never rewritten, when an API changes.
The candidate was authored after implementation consumers had begun and is therefore not accepted by the accompanying review transaction.
No exact historical comparator executable or root rustc/cargo binary identity was captured; old/new comparison remains blocked.
Performance rows define workloads and cleanup/resource invariants but do not invent unapproved latency thresholds.

expectations.subject: immutable migration replay and self-describing metamodel closure
expectations.rationale: A migration is accepted history; replay must create typed relation rows while predecessor mutation or bootstrap/model disagreement fails.
limitations: The fixture covers one relation declaration and predecessor edge, not the full initial model.

causal_controls.intervention: Replace predecessor m0 with an unrelated migration.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Replay rejects the chain before emitting model.relation.

expectations.subject: Tree-sitter raw node and grammar-native kind preservation
expectations.rationale: A function occurrence is a raw syntax node whose grammar kind and byte range must survive provider emission without becoming a semantic callable.
limitations: The single Python function does not exercise incremental edit reuse or every grammar node kind.

causal_controls.intervention: Relabel function_definition as callable_entity.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The raw-boundary expectation fails because syntax occurrence is not a semantic entity.

expectations.subject: Ruff recoverable parse diagnostics coexist with available typed syntax
expectations.rationale: parse_unchecked_source exposes recoverable parser state; diagnostics must not be converted into an empty successful fact set.
limitations: The fixture distinguishes recovery from rejection but does not enumerate every AST or trivia variant.

causal_controls.intervention: Drop the parser diagnostic and report complete coverage.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The expectation fails because malformed input cannot imply complete absence of facts.

expectations.subject: Pyrefly Query and TSP authority roles remain distinct
expectations.rationale: Bulk computed type comes from Query while declared and expected distinctions come from TSP; one facade cannot silently claim all roles.
limitations: This fixture does not cover Glean bulk declarations, LSP fallback, or project-specific module resolution.

causal_controls.intervention: Relabel the declared observation authority from TSP to Query.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The exact-surface authority expectation fails.

expectations.subject: rustc_public MIR facts are copied to owned rows inside the callback
expectations.rationale: MIR bodies and locals are public compiler facts, but rustc_public handles are callback-bound and cannot become durable application identity.
limitations: The fixture covers a simple return body and not monomorphization, closures, or trait-object dispatch.

causal_controls.intervention: Store a rustc_public Body or DefId handle beyond the callback.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Boundary validation rejects the row representation.

expectations.subject: narrow private seam owns stable-key and exact remainder only
expectations.rationale: StableCrateId plus DefPathHash and selected source or borrowck details may require rustc_private, while MIR and application dataflow remain outside that seam.
limitations: Private API availability is exact-nightly-specific and unsupported observations must remain explicit remainders.

causal_controls.intervention: Assign MIR body or application reaching-definitions authority to rustc_private.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Provider-family closure detects the authority expansion.

expectations.subject: failed provider coverage becomes explicit unknown and remainder
expectations.rationale: A compile or provider failure cannot leave stale-current semantic facts or make zero rows mean none.
limitations: The fixture models one failed rustc run; partial-family and cancellation trailers need additional release cases.

causal_controls.intervention: Report supported with an empty MIR relation after compile failure.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The absence-is-not-proof oracle fails.

expectations.subject: raw and normalized facts coexist through observation provenance
expectations.rationale: Normalization adds application meaning without erasing the provider-native kind or conflicting evidence.
limitations: One call node exercises coexistence but not multi-provider conflict resolution.

causal_controls.intervention: Erase raw_kind or set semantic_entity true without semantic resolution.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Normalization/provenance expectation fails.

expectations.subject: Python owner-local control, flow, alias, effect, resource, async, and pattern families
expectations.rationale: Application analyses, not syntax or Pyrefly, own these derived families and must expose conservative precision and provenance.
limitations: The family rows establish discriminating owner and semantics; release proof needs broader language constructs per family.

causal_controls.intervention: Delete the alternate reaching definition or relabel the producer Pyrefly.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Family semantics or producer-authority closure fails.

expectations.subject: Rust MIR-derived ownership, flow, alias, drop, async, unsafe, and call families
expectations.rationale: Owned raw MIR is input; CodeFabric analyses own derived flow and ownership rather than attributing them to rustc_public or the private seam.
limitations: The fixture is a simple move and drop; borrow regions, generators, and dynamic dispatch require release expansion.

decoded.source_utf8: fn f() { let s = String::new(); drop(s); }

causal_controls.intervention: Mark s available after the consuming drop call or claim rustc_private as derived owner.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Ownership semantics or authority closure fails.

expectations.subject: Common graph, control, summary, effect, resource, and metric families
expectations.rationale: Common analyses consume canonical relations and declare exact algorithm and precision rather than becoming hidden graph judgment.
limitations: The diamond graph does not exercise recursion, irreducible control flow, or large-graph resource behavior.

causal_controls.intervention: Add exit-to-entry and retain four singleton SCCs.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: SCC and reachability expectations discriminate the mutation.

expectations.subject: find entities compiles to the entities result role
expectations.rationale: The released form selects semantic entities with deterministic ordering and no physical identifiers.
limitations: One exact-name lookup does not cover phrase ambiguity or all filters.

causal_controls.intervention: Compile the block to raw table-name output.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Public result role/schema validation fails.

expectations.subject: retrieve facts compiles to the facts result role
expectations.rationale: Facts remain typed observations with provenance, not judgments.
limitations: One type fact does not cover every fact family.

causal_controls.intervention: Return an evaluative safe-to-refactor verdict.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Fact-only doctrine rejects the result.

expectations.subject: follow relationships preserves direction and bounded distance
expectations.rationale: Relationship traversal is bounded over semantic fact edges.
limitations: A one-hop call edge does not exercise cycles or stop predicates.

causal_controls.intervention: Reverse the requested direction without changing the result.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The relationship result differs or becomes empty.

expectations.subject: find paths returns ordered fact paths
expectations.rationale: Paths are ordered sequences, not unordered reachability sets.
limitations: The fixture has one shortest path and does not cover tie ordering.

causal_controls.intervention: Set maximum_length to one while retaining the two-edge path.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Bounded traversal rejects the retained path.

expectations.subject: match pattern returns bindings rather than judgment
expectations.rationale: Pattern matching exposes decoded variable bindings over fact relations.
limitations: One two-variable pattern does not cover optional or negative clauses.

causal_controls.intervention: Swap caller and callee binding roles.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Decoded binding equality fails.

expectations.subject: combine results consumes named upstream roles
expectations.rationale: Composition is an explicit DAG over prior blocks and roles, not string interpolation or arbitrary SQL.
limitations: A two-input union does not cover every composition operator.

causal_controls.intervention: Reference an unknown upstream block.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Composition resolution rejects the request before execution.

expectations.subject: summarize facts emits objective aggregates
expectations.rationale: Summaries are mechanically derived objective facts and preserve unknown coverage.
limitations: A count aggregate does not cover grouped numeric/null behavior.

causal_controls.intervention: Remove one input fact while retaining count two.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Aggregate equality fails.

expectations.subject: retrieve source context returns authorized bounded context
expectations.rationale: Source context is an explicit result role bounded by authorization and coordinates.
limitations: One authorized line does not cover truncation or unavailable source images.

causal_controls.intervention: Remove source authorization while retaining source bytes.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: The context becomes denied without leaking bytes.

expectations.subject: one epoch and semantics across internal, gRPC, resource, and FastMCP layers
expectations.rationale: Public delivery is accepted only when all four decoded layers refer to the same immutable epoch and logical rows.
limitations: The fixture does not exercise every stream frame or supported old client.

causal_controls.intervention: Change the FastMCP epoch or decoded row only.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Four-layer equality fails.

expectations.subject: unauthorized catalog, row, column, reference, and result identities are invisible
expectations.rationale: Authorization is construction of a reduced child catalog, not a post-query filter; metadata and errors cannot disclose hidden authority.
limitations: The fixture covers one denied workspace; OS credential and symlink races remain separate security cases.

causal_controls.intervention: Expose the hidden catalog name in the denial detail.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Metadata leakage oracle fails.

expectations.subject: untrusted build scripts and proc macros cannot escape the launcher
expectations.rationale: Rust semantic compilation is a policy-bearing trust boundary; unavailable containment must fail closed unless separately authorized trusted-local capability exists.
limitations: Platform containment requires OS-specific execution proof; this row defines expected denial, not proof that a backend exists.

causal_controls.intervention: Disable the network restriction while retaining a pass receipt.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Hostile containment probe detects the network effect and rejects proof.

expectations.subject: activation appends one predecessor-checked event and recovers by readback
expectations.rationale: Semantic current is derived from the Delta activation chain; a SQLite pointer or unproved epoch cannot override it.
limitations: The fixture covers one crash point after append and before in-memory swap.

causal_controls.intervention: Change the event predecessor to epoch-5 or recover from a SQLite current pointer.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Predecessor/readback proof fails.

expectations.subject: fenced cutover prevents the frozen legacy binary from serving or writing
expectations.rationale: Process stop is insufficient; external service/storage authority must reject a restarted old binary after target activation.
limitations: The row defines revocation semantics but cannot execute the missing historical binary.

causal_controls.intervention: Restore legacy storage credentials after target activation.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Exact old-binary restart probe can write and therefore fails cutover proof.

expectations.subject: bounded execution workload and cleanup invariants precede tuning
expectations.rationale: Admission, memory, spill, cancellation, backpressure, fairness, and result leases are correctness constraints measured on the real path before any performance policy changes.
limitations: No independently approved latency, throughput, or update-amplification numeric threshold exists in this candidate; a successor review must add one before performance release acceptance.

causal_controls.intervention: Ignore cancellation in one provider stream.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: Cleanup/resource proof observes retained work or lease and fails.
